reception: External reception is thinner than the project's own lineage: outside the group, BuildIt appears mostly as an entry in the multi-stage-programming canon. Papers from that community — on partially evaluating symbolic interpreters, on multi-stage evaluators with let-insertion, and on mechanized semantics of staging annotations — cite it as the C++ point in the design space, and SABLE lists it among staging frameworks for sparse computation. eCC++ positions its embedded-DSL framework against it directly, while systems such as SLANG.D, Flan, and Exo 2 mention it in passing as related infrastructure. The citations are few but come from the community the paper addresses. The framework lives on in the BuildIt-lang/buildit repository.
